title: intermittent-stability-sleuth-rohan
content:
Purpose / quick context:
- personal scratchpad for a weird intermittent regression surfaced across canary and main for the last 3 weeks. Not yet escalated to SRE — trying to isolate before opening a formal incident.
- Observed on: hosted-api (prod-edge-us) and aDedicated pool 3 (eu-west). Seems correlated with long-running sessions + mid-sequence context edits.
- Models touched: redwood-v2-large, redwood-v2-quantized-8bit, and a community-3b variant used for fallback.

High-level symptom (short):
- Occasionally (1 in ~2k requests) generation truncates early with a short sentinel token or repeats a 2-3 token loop then returns. For some prompts, output abruptly ends with a period or a trailing partial word.
- When it happens, latency is normal or slightly lower (weird). No obvious GPU OOMs, no host restarts logged in the same window.

Hypotheses (ranked quick list):
1) KV-cache eviction race with concurrent prefix updates — if prefix cached and a concurrent request rewrites cache, we may end up returning empty continuation. (P=0.45)
2) Batching micro-scheduling bug that merges short and long sequences incorrectly, causing decode step to zero-out beam state for some slots. (P=0.25)
3) Quantization kernel instability on certain sequence lengths (esp 512-640 tokens) causing token logit spikes -> early stop. (P=0.15)
4) Upstream prompt normalization change in API (trim/encode) causing subtle tokenization mismatch -> model generates sentinel and stops. (P=0.1)

Evidence gathered so far:
- Sample pool (50 positive reproductions attached below). Repro proportion: in canary with 2x higher sampling we see ~0.07% failure; in prod-edge we observed 0.05%. Dedicated pool shows 0.12% but skewed by smaller throughput.
- Request traces: 6 traces captured with full trace_id. None show worker reboots; kernel logs are clean. CPU usage normal.
- Token-level trace for one failing request shows final logits go extremely negative for all tokens except for a stop token id. (Could be quantization/overflow)
- When repeating failing input on same worker, occasionally it succeeds (non-deterministic) — argues for race or stateful cache issue.

Ad-hoc triage rubric (quick, to prioritize experiments):
- Repro Ease (E): can I reproduce locally / on canary with a small harness? (0-3)
- Surface (S): does it affect critical API paths or internal test-only flows? (0-3)
- Blast Radius (B): estimated user impact scaled by traffic to model route (0-4)
- Confidence (C): how confident is the prior/hypothesis after quick probe? (0-3)
- Score = (E*2 + S + B) * C  (toy scoring to order work)

Quick rubric entries (examples):
- Hypothesis 1 (KV eviction): E=2, S=3, B=3, C=2 -> Score=(4+3+3)*2=20
- Hypothesis 2 (Batch merge): E=1, S=3, B=3, C=1 -> Score=(2+3+3)*1=8
- Hypothesis 3 (Quant kernel): E=1, S=3, B=4, C=1 -> Score=(2+3+4)*1=9

Local experiments to run (ordered):
A) Repeat failing requests on single dedicated worker with KV-cache disabled (env: REDWOOD_KV_CACHE=off). Measure failure delta. (Why: isolate cache)
B) Force strict batching window (mini-batch sizes) to avoid mixing short+long. Environment override: INFER_BATCH_WINDOW_MS=1 and then 250 to see behavior.
C) Swap quantized kernel -> float fallback (QUANT_FALLBACK=true) and rerun failing inputs for 1000 iterations.
D) Re-run tokenization path with historical encoder version (tokenizer_v1 vs tokenizer_v2) to rule out normalization changes.

Sample failing requests (anonymized):
- Prompt A: "Summarize the policy changes for the upcoming fiscal quarter and suggest 3 implementation steps for the mobile team."
  - Expected: 4-6 bullet points with rationale.
  - Actual (fail): "...Implementation step 1.

." (single period + newline; generation ended)

- Prompt B: long conversation context (user edits earlier message mid-session), model returns: "Sure, here's the plan." then stops after 2 tokens.

Observations on token logs (one example):
- t=stepN, logits vector shows massive negative offsets except id 2 and id 50256 (stop). Softmax spikes to stop. Then sampler returns stop with high prob.
- Garbage collection events line up with one of the failing samples in the trace but not all.

Quick telemetry checklist to add to triage runbook:
- enable per-token logits dumping for route X for the next 24h (sample 1/10k)
- increase logging window around KV cache ops (annotate who invalidated)
- collect batch composition metrics: min/max seq length per batch, slot assignments
- surface quant kernel warnings flagged by CUDA profiler (if any)
- correlate failures with model revision / rollout timestamps

Notes about rollout correlation:
- New rollout (redwood-v2-large rev 3.2.1) deployed to canary on 2026-01-11; widened to prod on 2026-01-20. Failures existed before but spiked slightly after deploy. Not huge delta, but worth noting.

Short-term mitigation ideas (cheap):
- On route with high failure rate, temporarily pin to prev rev until root cause known. (Ops: low effort, immediate)
- Increase sampling for failed requests and automatically route flagged requests to float fallback.
- Soft kill: if sampler sees early stop < N tokens, re-run request with temperature=0.0 or sampling disabled and prefer topk.

Questions / open items I want to follow up with:
- Maya: can you share dedicated pool worker logs for 2026-02-18 02:00-04:00 UTC (I think one of the spike windows overlapped).
- Engineering: is there any kernel change in the quant rollout notes for 3.2.1? (rev link in GH artifact above)
- SRE: do we have any host-level preemptions or container recycling that correlate?

TODOs (short):
- [ ] Run experiment A and log result here (target: today)
- [ ] Add 24h per-token sampling for route X (owner: Rohan)
- [ ] Open small PR to add a protective check: if decode emits stop in first 3 tokens, attempt 1 automatic rerun (owner: Zoe)
- [ ] Draft incident if Score from rubric > 15 across multiple routes (owner: me)

Quick sign-off note: this doc is my personal triage workspace — verbose, partial hypotheses, rough scores. Will convert to a concise incident report if we escalate. Keep any sensitive client text out of the samples; I intentionally scrubbed.

Appendix: raw sample ids (for later paste into triage tool):
- trace-20260219-01-rcp9
- trace-20260223-17-rk3p
- trace-20260228-04-lm02

End of scratchpad.
